expectations.text: Both skill and agent created (a pair)
expectations.evidence: outputs contains exactly two authored artifacts forming the pair: .agents/skills/repo-triage/SKILL.md (trigger/interview/delegation skill) and .omp/agent/agents/repo-triage.md (task agent). The skill's '## Delegation' section spawns the repo-triage agent by name via the task tool, and the transcript confirms both writes with no scaffolding beyond the pair.

expectations.text: Agent frontmatter includes autoloadSkills naming omp-setup
expectations.evidence: repo-triage.md frontmatter line 5: `autoloadSkills: omp-setup` (scalar form, matching agent-craft's documented 'CSV of skill names' contract; omp accepts this form per omp://slash-command-internals.md:554 example).

expectations.text: Agent at home/.omp/agent/agents/repo-triage.md, skill at home/.agents/skills/
expectations.evidence: Verified on disk with outputs/ as fake HOME: outputs/.omp/agent/agents/repo-triage.md and outputs/.agents/skills/repo-triage/SKILL.md — the user-level layout agent-craft's install table prescribes.

expectations.text: Skill spells out the task-tool delegation contract
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md '## Delegation' opens 'spawn the **repo-triage** agent via the task tool' and gives an explicit task(context=..., tasks=[{ agent: "repo-triage", task: ..., solutionSpace: ... }]) block, then defines what context (repo root, read-only constraint, report shape), task (self-contained scope/focus/flags), and solutionSpace carry, plus '## Done looks like' specifying the six-section returned report — which agent, what to pass where, and what a finished job returns.

expectations.text: Agent has one-job statement and anti-jobs
expectations.evidence: One-job statement: 'you are the triage tech. one job: sweep a repo and return one honest report on what it is, how it's wired, and where it rots.' Anti-jobs present in substance (unlabeled): 'never install, never build, never commit, never edit anything, never spawn anything', 'bias to report, not fix', 'no files written to the repo'.

claims.claim: Agent tools limited to read, grep, glob, bash — no write/edit/task
claims.evidence: Frontmatter `tools: read, grep, glob, bash`; no write/edit/task present.

claims.claim: Model omitted so the agent inherits the parent session's model
claims.evidence: No model field in frontmatter; agent-craft SKILL.md documents omission = inherit in omp.

claims.claim: Skill written first, agent second, per the skill's workflow

claims.evidence: Full outputs tree is only the two files; nothing else under the fake HOME.

claims.claim: Preloaded omp-setup instructions are injected before the agent's first prompt
claims.evidence: Mechanism documented (omp://task-agent-discovery.md:47: autoloadSkills names skills injected before the first child prompt) and omp-setup exists at user level on this host (/home/x20/.agents/skills/omp-setup), so the name resolves; note omp silently ignores unknown names, and the run never verified resolvability itself.

suggestions.assertion: Agent at home/.omp/agent/agents/repo-triage.md, skill at home/.agents/skills/
suggestions.reason: Near-non-discriminating as written: any file at those paths passes. The baseline run passed this assertion by copying a pre-existing skill into home/.agents/skills/. Require content, e.g. skill frontmatter name = repo-triage and the skill referencing the agent by name.

suggestions.assertion: Agent has one-job statement and anti-jobs
suggestions.reason: Doesn't pin where the one-job statement and anti-jobs must live or their form. The baseline's lead agent passes on substance via an unlabeled '# Guardrails' section, while this run put the labeled '## Anti-jobs' section in the skill rather than the agent. Specify 'in the agent body' plus explicit prohibitions to remove grader judgment.

No assertion checks that the autoloaded skill actually resolves at user level. omp silently ignores unknown autoloadSkills names (omp://task-agent-discovery.md:47), so a typo'd preload would no-op invisibly. An assertion like 'the named skill exists under home/.agents/skills/ (or is a known canonical skill)' would catch silent preload failures — the baseline run did this check, this run did not.

No assertion covers read-only tool discipline on the agent (tools excluding write/edit), which is central to a triage agent's safety and which both runs implemented differently (read,grep,glob,bash vs read,grep,glob,find,bash,task).

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions all pass with genuine substance, but assertion 3 is satisfied by file placement alone and assertion 5 is under-specified; the eval's discriminating power currently rests on assertion 4.
